   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From: J.E. Hutchings, SOLIHULL

Dear Ron & Brian,

I'm very sorry and concerned
about the problem with OUTLET.
I, like many others I'm sure,
appreciate your hard work and
professionalism in producing
such a good quality product and
would be very upset if it were
to end. I would indeed not mind
paying more but I appreciate
there may be others who are not
able to do so.I think, however,
it's vital to maintain a month-
ly format.In respect to contrib-
utions, I for one do not require
any payments,simply to know they
are used is sufficient reward
and again I am sure there are


many like me. Obviously for some
who may spend many hours writing
their programs, there may be a
need for some sort of payment.


On a final point,I wonder if you
could help me with a problem
concerning the screens from
DEMOPIX. Having saved the pict-
ures as screen$ using the
prompts provided, I would then
like to re-use them in other
programs such as:-

- with Screen FX (Issue 60)


- To load 4 together and change
the display whilst playing a
SOUND MACHINE tune.

Unfortunately, because they are
compressed (I think) I can't get
4 to combine together and then
appear on the screen and more-
over I can't even get one on its
own to reappear after a CLS. Any
chance of some help with this?

All the best for the future,

        John Hutchings

Brian Cavers to John Hutchings


To use the routines from SCREEN
FX in last month's OUTLET you
need to study the listing from
10000 onwards and then experi-
ment by loading a screen and
calling the procedures. Study
also how the demos call the
procedures. You can only grasp
it by studying and experimenting
because it is not written as a
"shell" program for a user just
to press a few keys and use it
with his own screens - but for
programmers who can rewrite it
to suit themselves. At least,
that's the way I see it because
there are no instructions in it
explaining how to use it.

The basic principles of "fades"
and "merging" in screens is to
OPEN two screens, calculate the
address of each in memory and
use various POKEs to transfer
the one to the other in varying
patterns. To "fade" a screen you
would gradually transfer a blank
screen or just use PLOT and DRAW
to slowly erase the screen. You
can calculate the CURRENT screen
address by using LET SA=((IN 252
BAND 31)+1)*16384.You must first
"declare" that screen with e.g.,
SCREEN 3.A better way calculates
any screen address without show-
ing it... LET SCRN=((PEEK 23711+
SCRN No.) BAND 31)+1)*16384
Be prepared to experiment with
FOR NEXT loops etc. but SAVE any
lines you type before running!

In this month's issue should be
a program called "SHORELY NOT"
(if not, then next month) I have
put together with three screens
plus some music compiled using
the SOUND MACHINE program. You
might study that too. Note that
although the screens were comp-
ressed on the disc they are
expanded when the first load and
put into normal SCREEN positions
and their addresses calculated
as described. I then just
experimented with different
POKEs. Remember, on the SAM you
can POKE whole gulps of memory
not just one or two bytes, using
POKE A, MEM$(B TO C).I found the
maximum number of screens was 3
on a 256K machine because the
music uses several pages.

If you should compile any MUSIC+
SCREENS program using screens
from DEMOPIX then note that if
you contribute it to OUTLET I
would much prefer to use screens
that have not yet appeared in
OUTLET otherwise one is showing
the same screens. An exception
might be if the music matches
the screens in some way like my
SHORELY NOT program. I could
always add different screens or
I would be glad to let you have
some screens that have not been
published if you have some theme
in mind to go with some music.

Regarding including the music,
why not use my SHORELY NOT pro-
gram as a nucleus as it starts
and stops the music correctly
without resetting.

If you need any specific help in
programming just write again but
the main thing is to experiment!

If you load plain screens I can
compress them later.

Here's a simple example of one
screen in memory being made to
show on the screen after a CLS.

SCREEN 1: CLOSE SCREEN 2 (this
prevents errors on repeat)

OPEN SCREEN 2,4: SCREEN 2:
LOAD SCREEN (loads to SCREEN 2):

LET S2=((IN 252 BAND 31) ETC..
SCREEN 1: LET S1=((IN 252 ETC..
CLS: PAUSE    (press a key)
POKE S1,MEM$(S2 TO S2+24576)
                        - Brian

From: Graeme Tattersall, BELFAST


Could you give me details of how
to complete Level 3 of Prince of
Persia (SAM)? - that is, if you
or anyone else knows how to do
this. Level 3 is 'driving me up
the wall'!!!.

         Graeme Tattersall

B. Cavers to Graeme Tattershall

I've lent my copy to my sister
but this is the solution to
Level 3 as I remember it and I
shall correct myself next month
if I'm thinking of the wrong
level.

I think Level 3 is the one where
you have to climb a high tower
and run left across the "roofs"
of several "buildings" until you
see a closed gate at the left
across a wide chasm, right?

The switch to open the gate is
on top of the roof to the right
of where you climb up but it is
not easy to get back to the gate
before the gate closes again.

The method I used was to jump
across to the roof where the
switch is and stand facing right
with your feet half on the
switch (on the left edge of the
switch). You need to experiment
to get the exact position.

Make sure you have not got the
sound on your TV turned off and
you should hear the gate open in
the distance when you turn and
your heels click on the switch.
Now turn back to face right and
wait until you hear the gate
start to close. Quickly turn and
jump across the gap left and run
for your life! The action of
turning on the switch both re-
opens the gate but also I found
the "turn-and-jump" method
helped me not to jump wrongly.

As you race along the roofs you
have to jump the gaps and there
is one where I think you start
to jump almost before you enter
the screen. The final jump is
the hardest and you need to
practice to find the best point
to leap (on the run of course).
You have the advantage that you
can take it from me it IS
possible. When I did it I just
could not be sure that was the
way. I could not even reach the
screen with the gate before it
closed let alone reach the gate!
Sometimes you may leap and just
miss the gate but if you are
near enough you can grab the
foot of the gateway (I forget
the control to grab in flight).
If so,IMMEDIATELY start to climb
and you can get through.

Once through, it's relatively
easy and you do not need to
return the same way - there is
another way down to the exit.

Level 8 is also tough - as is
the very last level - but if you
persevere you should buckle all
your swashes with a bit of luck.
You can always write again.

By the way, I dropped my pen on
Level 7 so if you find it can
you post it to me next time?
Thanks.

                      - Brian

From: Malcolm Perry,
      KIDDERMINSTER

Firstly, many thanks to Cliff
Jackson for his idea on bringing
the drives forward. I had some a
while ago (in MGT days). I told
them there was a problem and I
then mentioned the PCB needed
slightly repositioning to re-
solve it. I have been putting up
with having to eject discs with
a pencil until I read the
letter, and so by removing the
rear screws and loosening the
front it was possible to slot
holes with a small round file
(make sure the filings do not
get into the works) by raising
the metal plate but not having
to disconnect keyboard tails.

On a different point:  printer
interfaces etc.tend to "hang" on
the rear connector. A stick on
foot centre back takes the
weight and stops it tending to
flop up and down.

Basil Lankester (Devon) said he
was having problems with using a
second drive at same time as
drive 1 but that an external
drive had been O.K. He wonders
if the current taken by the
drive has anything to do with it
as the external drive had its
own PSU. I consider he could
well be on the correct lines.
There is a separate article on
the subject of the PSU that I
consider relates to his problem.
[in a future DRIVECHAT - B.C.]

A test could be if a voltmeter
of reasonable accuracy and pref-
erably not a digital one as due
to their inherant count error
plus some delay while the meter
"counts" and settles to reading
makes them difficult to use for
this test.


Make up a lead with a plug to
fit either the PEN or SCART
sockets and connect two leads,
one to 0V (earth) and the second
to +5V. Connect to the voltmeter
on say 10V range, plug into the
computer, switch on, and note
the voltage. Now as various
combinations of disc operations
are carried out, take notice of
what the voltmeter is doing.

I do not recommend poking wires
into sockets to take readings as
there is all too easily the
chance of an accident.

If it behaves as described in
the item on the PSU then that
could well confirm the reason
for the problem.

All the best.

         Malcolm Perry

From: Basil Lankester, DEVON

I use "STYLEWRITER" on occasions
but find it a very slow printout
in the FONT mode -too, too slow.
I presume there is no way of
speeding it up?

I want to correct my statement
in my letter to you in OUTLET 60
on the subject of loading both
drives at once and getting a
corruption of the disc in drive
two.

What I forgot to say is that I
have an AUTOBOOT fitted and I
suspect this is what had caused
the problem when loading up both
discs at once, rather than any
faulty use of the RESET button.

Yes I agree "FLASH" is good
value, but I had got so used to
using either version of "ART
STUDIO" on the Speccy that I
find "FLASH" less elastic.

The MGT mouse is a bit too fast
for easy detail work. Sorry I
don't feel up to producing title
pages for you, I am in my
eighties and find coping with
work for a local parish magazine
about my limit. I wish I could
find a sensible way out of your
cash flow problems, but it seems
you are very sadly in an African
cleft stick position of a
difficult return! but I do wish
you lots of luck and many thanks
for your efforts so far with the
magazine.
               Basil Lankester

Brian Cavers to Basil Lankester

Yes, we have a review of the SC
AUTOBOOT soon and it does seem
that it does not cure the disc
corruption problem and is really
unusable on SAMs that corrupt
discs on reset because the disc
HAS to be on reset for AUTOBOOT
to work. I don't know what
percentage of SAMs suffer from
the problem but all 5 that I
know of do. I recommend you test
your SAM first before ordering
AUTOBOOT. Use a spare disc,
FORMAT it and save a few program
files on it. Now press RESET and
see if the files will load or if
you get a track/sector error. It
may not happen every time so you
need to repeat it many times to
be sure your machine is O.K.

Yes, FLASH is weak and slow in
many areas and the mouse version
is unusable for detailed work as
it jumps two or three pixels at
a time! However, I have heard
that someone has a new mouse
version that has cured this and
I'm trying to scrounge a copy.If
anyone has it then send it in!

Any routine using your printer's
graphics mode is bound to be
slow compared to normal printing
but a new STYLEWRITER is being
developed so perhaps some speed
improvement has been made. I
don't know yet. It can never be
as fast as your normal printer
speed of course.
                    - Brian

From: Marc Broster, LINCS.

Thanks for publishing my vector
text, anybody follow it? No, I
thought not. Anyway, if you
weren't convinced that rotation
is possible using a few simple
equations by my BASIC program -
enclosed is a machine code demo.
The demo rotates 'OUTLET' using
the equations I supplied in my
article. The distortion is
because of the inaccuracies in
my calculations.

To make things easier (Ever
tried floating point maths in
machine code? Without using the
ROM?) I took Sin 6 (0.104528) to
equal 0.1 and Cos 6 (0.994521)
to equal 1.

I didn't believe that such a
small error would make a lot of
difference, but it did. To test
this, I put together a small
Basic program. The white dots
are plotted using 0.1 and 1,
while the yellow dots are plot-
ted using the real values of Sin
6 and Cos 6. Can you think of a
way round this problem? Even
with the distortion, I'm quite
pleased with the demo, it's nice
and smooth, (I used shadow
screens) and quite fast, baring
in mind ROM routines are used.

On the subject of vectors, now
I've got the hang of them, I'd
quite like to try writing a
small game using wire frame
graphics, the only problem is

that I haven't got a decent line
draw routine, and I wondered if
you have ever published one in
OUTLET. In fact, it may be
faster to use a converted
Spectrum routine in Mode 1, then
again it may not.

On a different topic, I'am
trying to add sound effects to
my Columns game. I've read that
you use port 512 for the Sound
Chip address, and port 255 for
the data, but when I try to
produce a sound nothing happens,
even though sending the same
data using BASIC OUT statements
works fine. Have you managed to
use the sound chip from machine
code? Any help would be much
appreciated.      - Marc Broster

Brian Cavers to Marc Broster

Info on the sound chip from code
was in SAMCLASS 42 from Page 23
onwards. Here is an extracted
listing..
          LD HL, NOTETABLE
          LD C,255
          LD B,15
LOOP:     PUSH BC
          LD A,(HL)
          LD B,1
          OUT(C),A
          INC HL
          LD B,0
          LD A,(HL)
          OUT (C),A
          INC HL
          CALL WAIT
          POP BC
          DJNZ LOOP
          RET

NOTETABLE:DEFB 28,1,20,1
          DEFB 0,255,16,2,8,10,
          DEFB 8,20,8,40
          DEFB 8,80,8,100,8,120,
          DEFB 8,140
          DEFB 8,160,8,180,8,200
          DEFB 28,0

    WAIT: PUSH BC
          LD BC,32768
WAITLOOP: DEC BC
          LD A,B
          OR C
          JR NZ, WAITLOOP
          POP BC
          RET

More info in the SAMCLASS itself
but the above should get you
going.
                        - Brian

From:  William Easson, STOCKPORT

Dear Sirs,

My first Issue of OUTLET was
Issue 60 (I had tried Issue 40,
but insufficient funds prevented
me from subscribing). I'm sorry
to hear you're having financial
difficulties and think the
sanctions you have described
will go some way to alleviating
the situation. However, I
suggest you take up your old
system of allowing the readers
to supply their discs. You
needn't send the issues on the
exact disc they send (with the
number of readers you have this
would just over-complicate
things).

This would allow a decrease in
price while also cutting your
costs. As for raising the price,
I already subscribe to SAM
Supplement,am about to subscribe
to Enceladus and Arcadia; OUTLET
is already quite expensive, and
I don't think that I could
afford more than every alternate
issue, then ordering some back
issues if some money came my way
(I also have numerous other
hobbies to support).


From what I have read, it seems
that you are actually making a
living out of OUTLET, which also
drives up costs, so you will
have to create a bigger profit
margin somehow...

Enough of this. I was stunned to
hear (first in Your Sinclair
then in OUTLET 60) that SAMCo
had gone down. I am not
encouraged by talk of a buy out;
remember what happened to the
buy-out M.G.T had coming, but
never materialised? I'm probably
just cynical in my advancing
years, but I'm not too happy
about the whole situation. With
PBT going down too, all of our
SAM support is going. It's
depressing to say the least, but
read on... Flicking through the
pages of OUTLET, I noticed that
page 3 of the screen shots had a
topless model baring all on it.
I don't know whether this was a
ploy to raise sales or whatever
but I think it's quite tacky.

I'm a vehement opposer to
censorship at school (I'm always
having arguments in the Debating
Society about this), and I feel
that publications should do
their own vetting. However, the
page 3 model lowered my estimat-
ion of OUTLET somewhat. And no,
I'm not suggesting that younger
readers will be morally affected
etc. etc. a la Mary Whitehouse
(the detestable woman) and Co.,
but the Page 3 model is
unneccessary. Okay, just wait a
minute while I get off my
soapbox.

Back to SAMCo (R.I.P). I've
written to Alan Miles expressing
my regret, but I can't say it
was unexpected.

Even so, it took several
re-reads of Your Sinclair's SAM
Spot column for it to sink in
that it wasn't another puerile
joke of theirs, and that we had
lost what was surely the most
jinxed computer company yet. It
makes you wonder whether there
is some supernatural force
preventing the Coupe succeeding,
or whether all this is just
galvanising the Coupe community.

Incidentally, I am an atheist.
Why did I expect it? Well, I
read in SAM Supplement an issue
or two ago that SAMCo didn't
have any hardware in stock, for
some unknown reason. Nor did
they have any software, and they
couldn't fulfill orders.

Rumours were spreading that
sales of their new games 'Craft'
and 'Plasmoid' were astonish-
ingly low (confirmed in Your
Sinclair), and I started reading
a large number of letters dis-
satisfied with SAMCo's service.
A company operating like this
can't fulfill orders, no money
is moving through the company,
and generally, they were making
a pig's ear of operating.

I disagreed with a lot Alan
Miles was saying before SAMCo
went down, and I disagree with
him now; you CAN be a small
computer manufacturer, if you
get the scale of your business
right. SAMCo tried to grow too
quickly, as did MGT.

What Miles and Gordon should
have done, way back in 1989 when
the Coupe was produced, was keep
their computer peripheral lines
going; not only their Speccy
products, but also their Atari,
Ameagre (sorry; Amiga), and IBM
PC products (MGT did a mean
scanner with TEXT RECOGNITION
software for the latter), while
producing SAM on a much smaller
scale. Perhaps abandoning the
SAM custom case until the
computer got off the ground, and
putting the circuit board in a
ready-made IBM compatible case
and keyboard. But this is fine
to say in retrospect. They also
got two other things wrong, in
my opinion. Peripherals and
marketing..

Marketing; I didn't see any
adverts for the SAM; only
Spectrum owners knew about SAM,
they should also have advertised
further afield. The Guardian
Newspaper seemed to have a soft
spot for the SAM, as did the
late Popular Computing Weekly.

Peripherals. They tried too hard
to drive SAM into minority or
specialist niches; they should
have worked harder at developing
hardware which a large amount of
people would have wanted to buy.
A video digitiser is fine if you
use SAM in the same room as your
video, but I suspect most SAM
owners have their SAM several
rooms away from their video, and
using your SAM with a Camcorder

is fun for a little while, but
loses appeal after a few days.
Then they started talking
Genlocks; only for people who
are starting to get serious
about video editing. You need
something which ties all this
together; you've got video
snapshots, so what do you do
with them? How about a DTP
program? You can use digitised
pictures in those. PCG's DTP
programme can (the last I heard,
anyway) only load MODE 1
pictures. The pictures produced
by the digitiser are mode 4,
with 16 grey scales (64 with
Kaleidoscope).

Next, a decent printer driver.
Their efforts so far have been,

to say the least, crap. Bo
Jangeborg's efforts on FLASH!
were probably the best. 24 pin
printer drivers would have given
better resolution. SAMCo got it
right with MasterDOS, SAMBUS and
1MB upgrade, all tying in with
one another.

All of this is easy to say in
retrospect, but I was saying
this months ago, and nobody
listened...

Right. That's the doom and gloom
out of the way. Things, before
the SAMCo failure, were looking
upwards for SAM. We had a
dedicated parent company, we
still have a VERY talented user
base (Integrated Logic, Dr Andy

Wright, Dave Tonks and the
Supplement crew, Arcadia, Fred,
Enceladus, Entropy, to name but
a few), not to mention
dedicated; I doubt whether
Ameagre or Atari owners can
boast such, SEGA and NINTENDO
certainly can't. As soon as
something else becomes the rage,
they'll be dropped by the
public, but the SAM, the
Spectrum, Commodore 64,
Amstrads, the real fathers of
computing, they'll still be
there after God knows how long.
Still developing, being pushed
beyond their manufacturers
specifications. Then Ocean,
Domark, Microprose, etc. will
come begging for our custom to
keep THEM from receivership!

A dream? I don't think so.
Spectrum games sales (I'm
talking money made, as well as
unit sales) are still major
money earners for software
houses. Speccy format is still
the third best grossing format
after IBM and Amiga. So why are
the houses slowly dropping the
8-bit computers? The Amstrad and
Commodore have been hit far
harder than the Spectrum,
incidentally. It's the lack of
programmers willing to spend
three or four months programming
a Speccy game for a pittance,
when they could be earning far
more from the huge profit-
margins 16-bit games enjoy
because of their frilly graphics
and huge advertising budgets.

16-bit games are heavily
pirated, but still sell
reasonably large numbers.
Pirating on the Speccy is
estimated to be nearly
negligable, because of the low
cost of software (3 or four
pounds for a game with far more
gameplay than many 16-bit
titles). Public Domain is also
growing at a huge rate on 8-bit
computers. We on the SAM, as
well Amstrad owners have an
enormous choice. These are all
bedding us down for the years
ahead.

Oo-er! I sounded like a trade-
union fanatic, there! But
really, magazines and the
general press paint a grim

picture for the future of 8-bit
computing. But because we have
such a dedicated, loyal and
talented user base, the SAM and
Spectrum etc. can never die. The
only people who are going to
lose out are those people who
follow the press's whims on
what's in and what's not. Stick
with your SAM, and keep abreast
of what's happening, and you
can't go far wrong.

Thanks for OUTLET, and I hope
the money problems are sorted
out soon.

          Best Wishes,

         William Easson


PS! I'm sorry, but SAMScratch's
limited insert ability has made
me have to tack this on to the
end of this letter. Have you
considered dividing the task of
producing Outlet? SAM Supplement
has Dave Tonks putting the issue
together, while Brian Mumford
duplicates the magazine. Why not
do the same? You two produce and
put together the magazine, while
another outside person
duplicates the current issue and
handles subscription, while that
same person, or another person,
handles back issues, and
distribution of your other
products? It may sound a little
cumbersome, but in practice, it
could free a LOT of time for
jobs, school/college work, etc.

Brian Cavers to William Easson

We were LOSING money on the old
system of readers returning
their old discs for re-use. This
was because we HAD to obviously
offer this service at a lower
price than OUTLET on a new disc
and the costs of 3.5" discs is
now lower than any margin worth
considering. We offered OUTLET
at 50p less and yet we get bulk
discs for about 39p. In addition
we have extra costs, handling
the discs, checking, bad disc
problems, extra work involved in
INDIVIDUAL duplicating (as
against MASS duplicating in one
session)and all sorts of hassle.
With a new disc we just take an
OUTLET from stock.

It is likely that other existing
organisations will take over
different parts of SAMCo's
affairs. For instance, one or
different groups may take over
the software sales. Bruce Gordon
is continuing with hardware (see
LOOKOUT) and repairs and other
interested parties may supply
bits and pieces too. We shall
see. It is a long time since
Sinclair produced QL's but there
is still a thriving niche market
full of enthusiasts!

I note your views on our Page 3
girls but you will find in 1992
the vast majority of people in
the western world now accept
such harmless images without
concern.

If it's any consolation, our
supply of Page 3 girl screens
is now almost exhausted so they
may disappear or only appear
very occasionally unless more
are contributed.

As far as censoring ourselves,
yes, we do, and will not publish
screens that we feel the general
public in this country, in this
era,would find deeply offensive.

Your idea of dividing the work
of OUTLET is good but would cost
money (would YOU work FREE for a
commercial venture like CHEZRON)
and would not generate any more
cash sales. Remember, other disc
magazines do not declare profits
or keep accounts etc. but run it
as a "hobby".           - Brian

From: D. Scott, CARLISLE

Dear Brian and Ron,

It was sad to hear of the demise
of SAMCO, although not
completely unexpected. That is
sad, but if OUTLET were to go
under it would be tragic. There
can only be one answer -increase
the price. I only mention that I
am a pensioner to emphasize the
point that even as such, I
consider that an increase of
33.3% would not be too much.


Can you please tell me why the
justification in OUTWRITE
Version 1, does not work on the
first line of a new paragraph?

It is particularly obvious in
paragraph two of this letter.
[on the print-out] Perhaps
Version 2 will have cured this
quirk.

         Best wishes,

          David Scott

Brian Cavers to David Scott


Justification on the first line
of a paragraph did not work on
Version 1 of OUTWRITE because
you indented that line. This was
not allowed for in the first
version but it is O.K. in the
new version. However, note that
because ALL lines or part lines,
whether with spaces at the start
or not, are reformed into a
paragraph when REFORM PARAGRAPH
is used, any indentation is lost
if you reform from the top line.
This is inevitable with this
type of reforming because it
does not stop at a line with a
space at the start but only at a
totally blank line.

Ideally, the routine should have
tested for a blank line above to
determine the top of a paragraph
and inserted a few characters at
the start while it reformed then
removed them after. However,some
people do not leave a line space
between paragraphs and these are
the very ones who HAVE to indent
a paragraph to show where it is.

The only solution I can think of
is to do that manually by adding
a few X's at the start and then
removing them after reforming.
I agree it is not satisfactory
but inevitable with a REFORM
which removes ALL unnecessary
spaces (which far outweighs the
slight disadvantage to indent-
lovers!

There is another possibility
that I was pondering the other
week. Assuming you almost never
use the # (hash sign) then it
can be redefined as a space. If
you then enter a few hashes at
the start of paragraphs they
will print out as spaces. Again,
not brilliant but worth thinking
about. Any printer character may
be used of course but the # is
easier to type.

I must stress that indentation
with justification works fine -
it is only when reforming the
indent is lost. However in many
cases you need only reform from
the line below the top line so
it will not affect the indent.
                         - Brian

Brian Cavers to John Hutchings

To use the routines from SCREEN FX in last month's OUTLET you need to study the listing from 10000 onwards and then experi- ment by loading a screen and calling the procedures. Study also how the demos call the procedures. You can only grasp it by studying and experimenting because it is not written as a "shell" program for a user just to press a few keys and use it with his own screens - but for programmers who can rewrite it to suit themselves. At least, that's the way I see it because there are no instructions in it explaining how to use it.

The basic principles of "fades" and "merging" in screens is to OPEN two screens, calculate the address of each in memory and use various POKEs to transfer the one to the other in varying patterns. To "fade" a screen you would gradually transfer a blank screen or just use PLOT and DRAW to slowly erase the screen. You can calculate the CURRENT screen address by using LET SA=((IN 252 BAND 31)+1)*16384.You must first "declare" that screen with e.g., SCREEN 3.A better way calculates any screen address without show- ing it... LET SCRN=((PEEK 23711+ SCRN No.) BAND 31)+1)*16384 Be prepared to experiment with FOR NEXT loops etc. but SAVE any lines you type before running!

In this month's issue should be a program called "SHORELY NOT" (if not, then next month) I have put together with three screens plus some music compiled using the SOUND MACHINE program. You might study that too. Note that although the screens were comp- ressed on the disc they are expanded when the first load and put into normal SCREEN positions and their addresses calculated as described. I then just experimented with different POKEs. Remember, on the SAM you can POKE whole gulps of memory not just one or two bytes, using POKE A, MEM$(B TO C).I found the maximum number of screens was 3 on a 256K machine because the music uses several pages.

If you should compile any MUSIC+ SCREENS program using screens from DEMOPIX then note that if you contribute it to OUTLET I would much prefer to use screens that have not yet appeared in OUTLET otherwise one is showing the same screens. An exception might be if the music matches the screens in some way like my SHORELY NOT program. I could always add different screens or I would be glad to let you have some screens that have not been published if you have some theme in mind to go with some music.

Regarding including the music, why not use my SHORELY NOT pro- gram as a nucleus as it starts and stops the music correctly without resetting.

If you need any specific help in programming just write again but the main thing is to experiment!

If you load plain screens I can compress them later.

Here's a simple example of one screen in memory being made to show on the screen after a CLS.

SCREEN 1: CLOSE SCREEN 2 (this prevents errors on repeat)

OPEN SCREEN 2,4: SCREEN 2: LOAD SCREEN (loads to SCREEN 2):

LET S2=((IN 252 BAND 31) ETC.. SCREEN 1: LET S1=((IN 252 ETC.. CLS: PAUSE    (press a key) POKE S1,MEM$(S2 TO S2+24576)

```text
                        - Brian
```

From: Graeme Tattersall, BELFAST

Could you give me details of how to complete Level 3 of Prince of Persia (SAM)? - that is, if you or anyone else knows how to do this. Level 3 is 'driving me up the wall'!!!.

Graeme Tattersall

B. Cavers to Graeme Tattershall

I've lent my copy to my sister but this is the solution to Level 3 as I remember it and I shall correct myself next month if I'm thinking of the wrong level.

I think Level 3 is the one where you have to climb a high tower and run left across the "roofs" of several "buildings" until you see a closed gate at the left across a wide chasm, right?

The switch to open the gate is on top of the roof to the right of where you climb up but it is not easy to get back to the gate before the gate closes again.

The method I used was to jump across to the roof where the switch is and stand facing right with your feet half on the switch (on the left edge of the switch). You need to experiment to get the exact position.

Make sure you have not got the sound on your TV turned off and you should hear the gate open in the distance when you turn and your heels click on the switch. Now turn back to face right and wait until you hear the gate start to close. Quickly turn and jump across the gap left and run for your life! The action of turning on the switch both re- opens the gate but also I found the "turn-and-jump" method helped me not to jump wrongly.

As you race along the roofs you have to jump the gaps and there is one where I think you start to jump almost before you enter the screen. The final jump is the hardest and you need to practice to find the best point to leap (on the run of course). You have the advantage that you can take it from me it IS possible. When I did it I just could not be sure that was the way. I could not even reach the screen with the gate before it closed let alone reach the gate! Sometimes you may leap and just miss the gate but if you are near enough you can grab the foot of the gateway (I forget the control to grab in flight). If so,IMMEDIATELY start to climb and you can get through.

Once through, it's relatively easy and you do not need to return the same way - there is another way down to the exit.

Level 8 is also tough - as is the very last level - but if you persevere you should buckle all your swashes with a bit of luck. You can always write again.

By the way, I dropped my pen on Level 7 so if you find it can you post it to me next time? Thanks.

- Brian

From: Malcolm Perry, KIDDERMINSTER

Firstly, many thanks to Cliff Jackson for his idea on bringing the drives forward. I had some a while ago (in MGT days). I told them there was a problem and I then mentioned the PCB needed slightly repositioning to re- solve it. I have been putting up with having to eject discs with a pencil until I read the letter, and so by removing the rear screws and loosening the front it was possible to slot holes with a small round file (make sure the filings do not get into the works) by raising the metal plate but not having to disconnect keyboard tails.

On a different point:  printer interfaces etc.tend to "hang" on the rear connector. A stick on foot centre back takes the weight and stops it tending to flop up and down.

Basil Lankester (Devon) said he was having problems with using a second drive at same time as drive 1 but that an external drive had been O.K. He wonders if the current taken by the drive has anything to do with it as the external drive had its own PSU. I consider he could well be on the correct lines. There is a separate article on the subject of the PSU that I consider relates to his problem. [in a future DRIVECHAT - B.C.]

A test could be if a voltmeter of reasonable accuracy and pref- erably not a digital one as due to their inherant count error plus some delay while the meter "counts" and settles to reading makes them difficult to use for this test.

Make up a lead with a plug to fit either the PEN or SCART sockets and connect two leads, one to 0V (earth) and the second to +5V. Connect to the voltmeter on say 10V range, plug into the computer, switch on, and note the voltage. Now as various combinations of disc operations are carried out, take notice of what the voltmeter is doing.

I do not recommend poking wires into sockets to take readings as there is all too easily the chance of an accident.

If it behaves as described in the item on the PSU then that could well confirm the reason for the problem.

All the best.

Malcolm Perry

From: Basil Lankester, DEVON

I use "STYLEWRITER" on occasions but find it a very slow printout in the FONT mode -too, too slow. I presume there is no way of speeding it up?

I want to correct my statement in my letter to you in OUTLET 60 on the subject of loading both drives at once and getting a corruption of the disc in drive two.

Brian Cavers to Basil Lankester

Yes, we have a review of the SC AUTOBOOT soon and it does seem that it does not cure the disc corruption problem and is really unusable on SAMs that corrupt discs on reset because the disc HAS to be on reset for AUTOBOOT to work. I don't know what percentage of SAMs suffer from the problem but all 5 that I know of do. I recommend you test your SAM first before ordering AUTOBOOT. Use a spare disc, FORMAT it and save a few program files on it. Now press RESET and see if the files will load or if you get a track/sector error. It may not happen every time so you need to repeat it many times to be sure your machine is O.K.

Yes, FLASH is weak and slow in many areas and the mouse version is unusable for detailed work as it jumps two or three pixels at a time! However, I have heard that someone has a new mouse version that has cured this and I'm trying to scrounge a copy.If anyone has it then send it in!

From: Marc Broster, LINCS.

Thanks for publishing my vector text, anybody follow it? No, I thought not. Anyway, if you weren't convinced that rotation is possible using a few simple equations by my BASIC program - enclosed is a machine code demo. The demo rotates 'OUTLET' using the equations I supplied in my article. The distortion is because of the inaccuracies in my calculations.

To make things easier (Ever tried floating point maths in machine code? Without using the ROM?) I took Sin 6 (0.104528) to equal 0.1 and Cos 6 (0.994521) to equal 1.

I didn't believe that such a small error would make a lot of difference, but it did. To test this, I put together a small Basic program. Even with the distortion, I'm quite pleased with the demo, it's nice and smooth, (I used shadow screens) and quite fast, baring in mind ROM routines are used.

From:  William Easson, STOCKPORT

Dear Sirs,

My first Issue of OUTLET was Issue 60 (I had tried Issue 40, but insufficient funds prevented me from subscribing). I'm sorry to hear you're having financial difficulties and think the sanctions you have described will go some way to alleviating the situation. However, I suggest you take up your old system of allowing the readers to supply their discs. You needn't send the issues on the exact disc they send (with the number of readers you have this would just over-complicate things).

This would allow a decrease in price while also cutting your costs. As for raising the price, I already subscribe to SAM Supplement,am about to subscribe to Enceladus and Arcadia; OUTLET is already quite expensive, and I don't think that I could afford more than every alternate issue, then ordering some back issues if some money came my way (I also have numerous other hobbies to support).

From what I have read, it seems that you are actually making a living out of OUTLET, which also drives up costs, so you will have to create a bigger profit margin somehow...

Enough of this. I was stunned to hear (first in Your Sinclair then in OUTLET 60) that SAMCo had gone down. I am not encouraged by talk of a buy out; remember what happened to the buy-out M.G.T had coming, but never materialised? I'm probably just cynical in my advancing years, but I'm not too happy about the whole situation. With PBT going down too, all of our SAM support is going. It's depressing to say the least, but read on... Flicking through the pages of OUTLET, I noticed that page 3 of the screen shots had a topless model baring all on it. I don't know whether this was a ploy to raise sales or whatever but I think it's quite tacky.

I'm a vehement opposer to censorship at school (I'm always having arguments in the Debating Society about this), and I feel that publications should do their own vetting. However, the page 3 model lowered my estimat- ion of OUTLET somewhat. And no, I'm not suggesting that younger readers will be morally affected etc. etc. a la Mary Whitehouse (the detestable woman) and Co., but the Page 3 model is unneccessary. Okay, just wait a minute while I get off my soapbox.

Back to SAMCo (R.I.P). I've written to Alan Miles expressing my regret, but I can't say it was unexpected.

Even so, it took several re-reads of Your Sinclair's SAM Spot column for it to sink in that it wasn't another puerile joke of theirs, and that we had lost what was surely the most jinxed computer company yet. It makes you wonder whether there is some supernatural force preventing the Coupe succeeding, or whether all this is just galvanising the Coupe community.

Incidentally, I am an atheist. Why did I expect it? Well, I read in SAM Supplement an issue or two ago that SAMCo didn't have any hardware in stock, for some unknown reason. Nor did they have any software, and they couldn't fulfill orders.

Rumours were spreading that sales of their new games 'Craft' and 'Plasmoid' were astonish- ingly low (confirmed in Your Sinclair), and I started reading a large number of letters dis- satisfied with SAMCo's service. A company operating like this can't fulfill orders, no money is moving through the company, and generally, they were making a pig's ear of operating.

I disagreed with a lot Alan Miles was saying before SAMCo went down, and I disagree with him now; you CAN be a small computer manufacturer, if you get the scale of your business right. SAMCo tried to grow too quickly, as did MGT.

What Miles and Gordon should have done, way back in 1989 when the Coupe was produced, was keep their computer peripheral lines going; not only their Speccy products, but also their Atari, Ameagre (sorry; Amiga), and IBM PC products (MGT did a mean scanner with TEXT RECOGNITION software for the latter), while producing SAM on a much smaller scale. Perhaps abandoning the SAM custom case until the computer got off the ground, and putting the circuit board in a ready-made IBM compatible case and keyboard. But this is fine to say in retrospect. They also got two other things wrong, in my opinion. Peripherals and marketing..

Marketing; I didn't see any adverts for the SAM; only Spectrum owners knew about SAM, they should also have advertised further afield. The Guardian Newspaper seemed to have a soft spot for the SAM, as did the late Popular Computing Weekly.

Peripherals. They tried too hard to drive SAM into minority or specialist niches; they should have worked harder at developing hardware which a large amount of people would have wanted to buy. A video digitiser is fine if you use SAM in the same room as your video, but I suspect most SAM owners have their SAM several rooms away from their video, and using your SAM with a Camcorder

is fun for a little while, but loses appeal after a few days. Then they started talking Genlocks; only for people who are starting to get serious about video editing. You need something which ties all this together; you've got video snapshots, so what do you do with them? How about a DTP program? You can use digitised pictures in those. PCG's DTP programme can (the last I heard, anyway) only load MODE 1 pictures. The pictures produced by the digitiser are mode 4, with 16 grey scales (64 with Kaleidoscope).

Next, a decent printer driver. Their efforts so far have been,

to say the least, crap. Bo Jangeborg's efforts on FLASH! were probably the best. 24 pin printer drivers would have given better resolution. SAMCo got it right with MasterDOS, SAMBUS and 1MB upgrade, all tying in with one another.

All of this is easy to say in retrospect, but I was saying this months ago, and nobody listened...

Right. That's the doom and gloom out of the way. Things, before the SAMCo failure, were looking upwards for SAM. We had a dedicated parent company, we still have a VERY talented user base (Integrated Logic, Dr Andy

Wright, Dave Tonks and the Supplement crew, Arcadia, Fred, Enceladus, Entropy, to name but a few), not to mention dedicated; I doubt whether Ameagre or Atari owners can boast such, SEGA and NINTENDO certainly can't. As soon as something else becomes the rage, they'll be dropped by the public, but the SAM, the Spectrum, Commodore 64, Amstrads, the real fathers of computing, they'll still be there after God knows how long. Still developing, being pushed beyond their manufacturers specifications. Then Ocean, Domark, Microprose, etc. will come begging for our custom to keep THEM from receivership!

A dream? I don't think so. Spectrum games sales (I'm talking money made, as well as unit sales) are still major money earners for software houses. Speccy format is still the third best grossing format after IBM and Amiga. So why are the houses slowly dropping the 8-bit computers? The Amstrad and Commodore have been hit far harder than the Spectrum, incidentally. It's the lack of programmers willing to spend three or four months programming a Speccy game for a pittance, when they could be earning far more from the huge profit- margins 16-bit games enjoy because of their frilly graphics and huge advertising budgets.

16-bit games are heavily pirated, but still sell reasonably large numbers. Pirating on the Speccy is estimated to be nearly negligable, because of the low cost of software (3 or four pounds for a game with far more gameplay than many 16-bit titles). Public Domain is also growing at a huge rate on 8-bit computers. We on the SAM, as well Amstrad owners have an enormous choice. These are all bedding us down for the years ahead.

Oo-er! I sounded like a trade- union fanatic, there! But really, magazines and the general press paint a grim

picture for the future of 8-bit computing. But because we have such a dedicated, loyal and talented user base, the SAM and Spectrum etc. can never die. The only people who are going to lose out are those people who follow the press's whims on what's in and what's not. Stick with your SAM, and keep abreast of what's happening, and you can't go far wrong.

Thanks for OUTLET, and I hope the money problems are sorted out soon.

Best Wishes,

William Easson

PS! I'm sorry, but SAMScratch's limited insert ability has made me have to tack this on to the end of this letter. Have you considered dividing the task of producing Outlet? SAM Supplement has Dave Tonks putting the issue together, while Brian Mumford duplicates the magazine. Why not do the same? You two produce and put together the magazine, while another outside person duplicates the current issue and handles subscription, while that same person, or another person, handles back issues, and distribution of your other products? It may sound a little cumbersome, but in practice, it could free a LOT of time for jobs, school/college work, etc.

Brian Cavers to William Easson

We were LOSING money on the old system of readers returning their old discs for re-use. This was because we HAD to obviously offer this service at a lower price than OUTLET on a new disc and the costs of 3.5" discs is now lower than any margin worth considering. We offered OUTLET at 50p less and yet we get bulk discs for about 39p. In addition we have extra costs, handling the discs, checking, bad disc problems, extra work involved in INDIVIDUAL duplicating (as against MASS duplicating in one session)and all sorts of hassle. With a new disc we just take an OUTLET from stock.

It is likely that other existing organisations will take over different parts of SAMCo's affairs. For instance, one or different groups may take over the software sales. Bruce Gordon is continuing with hardware (see LOOKOUT) and repairs and other interested parties may supply bits and pieces too. We shall see. It is a long time since Sinclair produced QL's but there is still a thriving niche market full of enthusiasts!

I note your views on our Page 3 girls but you will find in 1992 the vast majority of people in the western world now accept such harmless images without concern.

If it's any consolation, our supply of Page 3 girl screens is now almost exhausted so they may disappear or only appear very occasionally unless more are contributed.

As far as censoring ourselves, yes, we do, and will not publish screens that we feel the general public in this country, in this era,would find deeply offensive.

Your idea of dividing the work of OUTLET is good but would cost money (would YOU work FREE for a commercial venture like CHEZRON) and would not generate any more cash sales. Remember, other disc magazines do not declare profits or keep accounts etc. but run it as a "hobby".           - Brian

From: D. Scott, CARLISLE

Dear Brian and Ron,

Brian Cavers to David Scott

Justification on the first line of a paragraph did not work on Version 1 of OUTWRITE because you indented that line. This was not allowed for in the first version but it is O.K. in the new version. However, note that because ALL lines or part lines, whether with spaces at the start or not, are reformed into a paragraph when REFORM PARAGRAPH is used, any indentation is lost if you reform from the top line. This is inevitable with this type of reforming because it does not stop at a line with a space at the start but only at a totally blank line.

Ideally, the routine should have tested for a blank line above to determine the top of a paragraph and inserted a few characters at the start while it reformed then removed them after. However,some people do not leave a line space between paragraphs and these are the very ones who HAVE to indent a paragraph to show where it is.

The only solution I can think of is to do that manually by adding a few X's at the start and then removing them after reforming. I agree it is not satisfactory but inevitable with a REFORM which removes ALL unnecessary spaces (which far outweighs the slight disadvantage to indent- lovers!

There is another possibility that I was pondering the other week. Assuming you almost never use the # (hash sign) then it can be redefined as a space. If you then enter a few hashes at the start of paragraphs they will print out as spaces. Again, not brilliant but worth thinking about. Any printer character may be used of course but the # is easier to type.

I must stress that indentation with justification works fine - it is only when reforming the indent is lost. However in many cases you need only reform from the line below the top line so it will not affect the indent.

**Brian Cavers отвечает John Hutchings:**

Чтобы использовать подпрограммы из SCREEN FX из прошлого номера OUTLET, вам нужно изучить листинг со строки 10000 и далее, а затем поэкспериментировать, загружая экран и вызывая процедуры. Посмотрите также, как процедуры вызываются в демо-версиях. Разобраться в этом можно только путем изучения и экспериментов, поскольку программа написана не как «оболочка», где пользователю достаточно нажать пару клавиш и подставить свои экраны, а для программистов, способных переписать ее под себя. По крайней мере, именно так я это вижу, поскольку никаких инструкций по использованию внутри нет.

Базовый принцип «фейдов» и «слияний» экранов заключается в том, чтобы сделать OPEN двух экранов, рассчитать адрес каждого в памяти и использовать различные POKE для переноса данных из одного в другой по различным шаблонам. Чтобы экран плавно «растворился» (fade), можно постепенно переносить пустой экран или просто использовать PLOT и DRAW, чтобы медленно очистить его. Адрес ТЕКУЩЕГО экрана можно рассчитать так: `LET SA=((IN 252 BAND 31)+1)*16384`. Сначала вы должны «объявить» этот экран, например, с помощью `SCREEN 3`. Более удобный способ вычисляет адрес любого экрана без его показа... `LET SCRN=((PEEK 23711+SCRN No.) BAND 31)+1)*16384`. Будьте готовы поэкспериментировать с циклами FOR NEXT и т.д., но обязательно сохраняйте набранные строки перед запуском!

В этом номере должна быть программа под названием "SHORELY NOT" (если нет, то в следующем), которую я собрал из трех экранов плюс музыка, скомпилированная с помощью программы SOUND MACHINE. Вы могли бы изучить и ее. Обратите внимание: хотя экраны на диске были сжаты, они разворачиваются при первой загрузке и помещаются в стандартные позиции SCREEN, а их адреса вычисляются описанным способом. Затем я просто экспериментировал с различными POKE. Помните, что на SAM можно отправлять через POKE целые массивы памяти, а не только по одному-два байта, используя `POKE A, MEM$(B TO C)`. Я выяснил, что максимальное количество экранов — 3 на машине с 256K, поскольку музыка занимает несколько страниц.

Если вы скомпилируете какую-нибудь программу МУЗЫКА+ЭКРАНЫ с использованием графики из DEMOPIX, то учтите: если вы решите отправить ее в OUTLET, я предпочел бы использовать экраны, которые еще не появлялись в журнале, иначе придется показывать одно и то же. Исключением может быть случай, когда музыка тематически идеально подходит к экранам, как в моей программе SHORELY NOT. Я всегда могу добавить другие экраны, или с удовольствием поделюсь с вами неопубликованными картинками, если у вас есть определенная тема под конкретную музыку.

Что касается добавления музыки: почему бы не взять мою программу SHORELY NOT за основу? Она корректно запускает и останавливает музыку без перезагрузки.

Если вам понадобится конкретная помощь по программированию, просто напишите еще раз, но главное — экспериментируйте!

Если вы загружаете несжатые экраны, я могу сжать их позже.

Вот простой пример того, как экран, находящийся в памяти, выводится на дисплей после команды CLS:

```text
SCREEN 1: CLOSE SCREEN 2 (это предотвратит ошибки при повторном запуске)

OPEN SCREEN 2,4: SCREEN 2:
LOAD SCREEN (загрузка в SCREEN 2):

LET S2=((IN 252 BAND 31) И Т.Д..
SCREEN 1: LET S1=((IN 252 И Т.Д..
CLS: PAUSE    (нажмите клавишу)
POKE S1,MEM$(S2 TO S2+24576)
```
— Brian

**B. Cavers отвечает Graeme Tattershall:**

Я одолжил свою копию сестре, но вот прохождение 3-го уровня по памяти, и я поправлюсь в следующем месяце, если перепутал уровни.

Кажется, Уровень 3 — это тот, где нужно взобраться на высокую башню и бежать влево по «крышам» нескольких «зданий», пока не увидите закрытые ворота слева за широкой пропастью, верно?

Переключатель, открывающий ворота, находится на вершине крыши справа от того места, где вы залезаете, но вернуться к воротам до того, как они снова закроются, очень непросто.

Я делал так: перепрыгивал на крышу, где находится переключатель, и вставал лицом вправо так, чтобы ступни наполовину стояли на переключателе (на левом его краю). Придется поэкспериментировать, чтобы найти точное положение.

Убедитесь, что звук на телевизоре включен, и вы должны услышать, как вдалеке открываются ворота, когда вы поворачиваетесь и ваши пятки щелкают по переключателю. Теперь снова повернитесь лицом вправо и подождите, пока не услышите, что ворота начали закрываться. Быстро разворачивайтесь, прыгайте через пропасть влево и бегите изо всех сил! Поворот на переключателе не только снова открывает ворота, но также, как я заметил, метод «повернулся-и-прыгнул» помогает не сорваться при прыжке.

Пока вы мчитесь по крышам, вам нужно перепрыгивать пропасти, и в одном месте, кажется, прыжок нужно начинать чуть ли не до того, как вы выбежите на экран. Финальный прыжок — самый сложный, и нужно потренироваться, чтобы найти лучшую точку для прыжка (естественно, с разбега). Ваше преимущество в том, что вы знаете от меня: это ВОЗМОЖНО. Когда я проходил сам, я не был уверен, что путь именно этот. Я даже не успевал добежать до экрана с воротами до того, как они захлопнутся, не говоря уже о самих воротах! Иногда вы можете прыгнуть и чуть-чуть не долететь, но если будете достаточно близко, можно ухватиться за порог проема ворот (я забыл кнопку, отвечающую за захват в полете). Если получилось — НЕМЕДЛЕННО начинайте карабкаться, и вы проскочите.

Как только пройдете ворота, дальше будет относительно легко, и возвращаться тем же путем не придется — к выходу ведет другой спуск.

Уровень 8 тоже очень сложный — как и самый последний уровень, — но если проявите упорство и немного удачи, победа будет за вами. Вы всегда можете написать нам снова.

Кстати, я уронил свою ручку на 7-м уровне, так что если найдете ее, пришлете мне почтой в следующий раз? Спасибо.

— Brian

**От: Malcolm Perry, KIDDERMINSTER**

Во-первых, огромное спасибо Cliff Jackson за его идею выдвинуть дисководы вперед. У меня такое было некоторое время назад (еще во времена MGT). Я сказал им, что есть проблема, а затем упомянул, что для ее решения нужно немного изменить положение печатной платы. До прочтения письма мне приходилось мириться с тем, что диски приходилось извлекать карандашом, но, выкрутив задние винты и ослабив передние, удалось сделать пропилы круглым напильником (следите, чтобы опилки не попали в механизм), приподняв металлическую пластину и не отсоединяя шлейфы клавиатуры.

И еще по другому поводу: интерфейсы принтеров и т.д. имеют тенденцию «провисать» на заднем разъеме. Самоклеящаяся ножка по центру сзади принимает на себя вес и не дает разъему болтаться вверх и вниз.

Basil Lankester (Devon) упомянул, что у него возникают проблемы при одновременном использовании второго дисковода с первым, но с внешним дисководом все было в порядке. Он предполагает, не связано ли это с потребляемым дисководом током, поскольку у внешнего дисковода был свой собственный блок питания. Полагаю, он вполне может быть на верном пути. Есть отдельная статья на тему БП, которая, как мне кажется, имеет прямое отношение к его проблеме. [в одном из следующих выпусков DRIVECHAT — B.C.]

Для проверки можно использовать вольтметр с приемлемой точностью, причем лучше не цифровой — из-за присущей им погрешности дискретизации плюс задержки, пока прибор «считает» и стабилизирует показания, их трудно использовать для этого теста.

Сделайте шнур с разъемом под гнездо PEN или SCART и выведите два провода: один к 0V (земля), второй к +5V. Подключите к вольтметру (скажем, на пределе 10V), вставьте в компьютер, включите и запишите напряжение. Теперь, выполняя различные комбинации дисковых операций, обращайте внимание на то, что показывает вольтметр.

Я не рекомендую тыкать проводами прямо в разъемы для снятия показаний, так как слишком велик риск замкнуть что-нибудь.

Если прибор ведет себя так, как описано в заметке о БП, это вполне может подтвердить причину неполадок.

Всего наилучшего.

Malcolm Perry

### Brian Cavers — Basil Lankester

Да, у нас скоро будет обзор на SC AUTOBOOT, и, судя по всему, он не устраняет проблему с порчей дисков и совершенно непригоден для SAM'ов, которые портят диски при сбросе, поскольку для работы AUTOBOOT диск ОБЯЗАН быть вставлен в момент сброса. Не знаю, какой процент SAM'ов страдает этой проблемой, но все 5 известных мне машин ей подвержены. Я рекомендую сначала протестировать свой SAM, прежде чем заказывать AUTOBOOT. Возьмите чистый диск, сделайте FORMAT и сохраните на него несколько программ. Затем нажмите RESET и проверьте, загружаются ли файлы или вылетает ошибка трека/сектора. ### Brian Cavers отвечает David Scott

Выравнивание по ширине первой строки абзаца не работало в Version 1 программы OUTWRITE из-за того, что вы делали отступ (красную строку). Это не было предусмотрено в первой версии, но прекрасно работает в новой. Однако учтите: поскольку при использовании REFORM PARAGRAPH ВСЕ строки или их части (независимо от того, есть ли пробелы в начале или нет) переформатируются в один абзац, любой отступ будет потерян, если вы начнете переформатирование с самой верхней строки. При таком типе форматирования это неизбежно, так как процедура не останавливается на строке с пробелом в начале, а реагирует только на полностью пустую строку.

В идеале процедура должна была проверять наличие пустой строки сверху, чтобы определить начало абзаца, вставлять несколько символов в начало на время форматирования, а затем удалять их. Однако некоторые люди не оставляют пустую строку между абзацами, и именно им ПРИХОДИТСЯ делать отступ, чтобы показать, где он начинается.

Единственное решение, которое я могу придумать — делать это вручную: добавить пару символов «X» в начале, а после переформатирования стереть их. Согласен, решение не идеальное, но неизбежное при наличии функции REFORM, которая удаляет ВСЕ лишние пробелы (что с лихвой перевешивает небольшое неудобство для любителей красных строк!).

На днях я размышлял над еще одной возможностью. Если вы почти никогда не используете символ # (решетку), его можно переопределить как пробел.
